pairs: A Distribution and Measurement of a Proposed Study
Undergraduate course teaching example: Compare step-by-step prompts and complete answers, with the score of new questions without AI after one week as the main result.
No new AI questions after one week
Similar content and time rules; supplementary records of on-site performance, time taken and additional help.
Teaching simulation: 50 people/group from hypothetical scenario on page 11; not yet recruited, collected or approved.
items.note:
This page develops the proposed problem into a design that can be discussed. It is assumed that individual students are used as independent allocation units. After completing the baseline measurement, students are randomly assigned to two conditions: step-by-step prompts and complete answers on a 1:1 basis. The two groups used the same content, the same time rules and measurement arrangements to record sharing, extra help and absences between classmates. Individual independence and mutual influence can be ignored. Currently, it is only a prerequisite for calculation and must be verified before starting. If the allocation is ultimately based on classes, the number of people on this page cannot be used directly.
The main results are planned to be 5 new questions under no AI conditions after one week, with a total score of 0-100; the scoring rules of 0-20 for each question, question equivalence and rater consistency need to be formed and evaluated first. The week, number of questions, and point scale are proposed settings for teaching and are not validated measurement protocols derived from published papers. The baseline is only a record of the previous level, and the on-site performance and usage time are supplementary results. The main problem cannot be replaced after the main results are unsatisfactory.
The figure above plans to recruit 50 people into each group, which comes from the conditional calculation of "difference 6 points, standard deviation 10 points, two-sided 0.05, power 80%, hypothesis retention 90%" on page 11. This is to show how the parameters affect the plan. It is not recommended to use this scenario directly as a formal sample basis. It is expected that each group will retain 45 complete primary results, but there is no guarantee that 45 will actually be reached. If it is still insufficient after reaching the predetermined deadline, the actual accuracy and detectable range should be stated, and the sample cannot be expanded while watching the results.
The main analysis is to compare the mean difference in scores one week after the two groups are assigned and report the range; the assigned personnel will remain registered according to the original grouping, and those who have not measured the results will be marked as missing. The current power calculation only addresses the simplified scenario of no clustering, equal variances, two sets of independent t-tests, and does not address actual missing treatments, interference, or scale quality. The formal analysis plan needs to clarify the missing and exclusion processing and sensitivity analysis before the results appear, and be reviewed and approved by the researcher.

If the treatment is applied to an entire batch of material, the individual allocation unit may be the batch and the specimens may not automatically be treated as independent replicates. Technical replicates and independent replicates are determined at the actual level of preparation, distribution, and measurement; analyzes may need to deal with nested correlations.

items.note:
Blinding requires specifying whose information is being withheld. It is sometimes impossible for the lecturer or subject to be unaware of the intervention, but the rater may still be unaware of the groupings. Don’t just make anonymous numbers so that all participants are blinded. Blind destruction, exception handling and decoding times need to be documented. This page is a method description and does not claim that the examples have been double-blinded.
